title: Hosted API microburst buffer plan and peak-window projections (2029Q1)
body:
Purpose:
Short working spreadsheet to translate observed short-window peaks (1–15m) into concrete GPU-slice headroom targets and prewarm+fallback rules for the Hosted API. This is intentionally compact — aims to align infra, SRE, and product on a single microburst mitigation heuristic before we drop into detailed provisioning tables.

Key goals:
- Define 1m / 5m / 15m headroom targets (tokens/sec and QPS) by region and GPU family.
- Provide quick conversion rules to estimate required GPU slices for different model classes (small/medium/large gen).
- Recommend prewarm and burst strategies (pre-slice, ephemeral burst, cross-region spill).
- Surface actionable TODOs + tickets for automating prewarm and metrics.

Assumptions and knobs (rough):
- Average token cost per request: small models = 50 tokens, med = 150 tokens, large = 600 tokens (these are conservative for peak calc).
- Typical peak composition: 60% small, 30% med, 10% large for consumer-facing apps; enterprise customers skew heavier to med/large.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU-slice (baseline):
  - A100-80GB (gen-v1 slice): 140k tokens/sec
  - H100-80GB (gen-v2 slice): 220k tokens/sec
  - L4-48GB (inference-optimized): 45k tokens/sec
  (these reflect quantized mixed-precision tuned workloads — measure in linked PRs).
- Target utilization goal (steady-state): 55–65% to leave headroom for request variance and KV-cache churn.

Summary projection table (1m peak, 5m rolling, 15m rolling) [CSV-ish rows]:
Region,1m_peak_tokens/sec,5m_rsvp_tokens/sec,15m_rsvp_tokens/sec,preferred_gpu_family,1m_headroom_pct,5m_headroom_pct,15m_headroom_pct
us-west1,1,140,000,1,060,000,920,000,H100,40,30,20
us-east4,92000,70000,58000,A100,45,32,22
eu-west1,78,000,62,000,52,000,H100,50,35,25
ap-northeast1,36,000,28,000,24,000,L4,60,40,25
sa-east1,8,500,6,200,5,000,A100,70,50,35

Notes on table above:
- Values are illustrative: 1m_peak = observed 99th percentile single-minute token rate over the trailing 30 days. 5m/15m are rolling aggregates used to size autoscaling cooldowns.
- Headroom_pct is the target buffer to provision above observed peak to avoid throttling during microbursts. Higher for smaller regions.

Quick conversion examples (how to map tokens/sec requirement -> slices):
- Example A: us-west1 1m_peak 1.14M tokens/sec, prefer H100 (220k tokens/sec per-slice). Required slices = ceil(1.14M / (220k * target_utilization)). With util=0.6 -> slices = ceil(1.14M / 132k) = 9 slices. Apply headroom_pct 40% -> provision = ceil(9 * 1.4) = 13 slices.
- Example B: eu-west1 1m_peak 78k tokens/sec on H100 -> slices at 60% util = ceil(78k / 132k) = 1 slice; with 50% headroom -> 2 slices.

Recommended immediate actions (short-term, 0–30d):
- ACTION-1: Instrument 1m/5m/15m per-route token-rate (already in metrics backlog JIRA-INFRA-8421). Need an SLO tag for routes that are "burst-sensitive".
- ACTION-2: Implement a prewarm policy that maintains N spare slices per-region: formula N = max(1, round(peak_slice_estimate * prewarm_ratio)). Default prewarm_ratio = 0.12 (12%).
- ACTION-3: Add ephemeral burst pool (cross-region) with fast cold-start allowed (30–90s) — only used if prewarm pool is exhausted.

Prewarm math illustrative table:
Region,peak_slices_est,prewarm_ratio,prewarm_slices(default)
us-west1,9,0.12,2
eu-west1,1,0.12,1
ap-northeast1,2,0.12,1
sa-east1,1,0.2,1

Fallback and degradation policy (behavioral guidance):
- Primary: cool down to lower-capacity model variant (quantized/4-bit) within same family if latency SLO allows (trigger threshold = sustained >120s over headroom).
- Secondary: cross-region spill to nearest healthy region (pay attention to cross-region latency and data residency flags).
- Last resort: token-budget based shedding (start with background tasks / non-interactive requests).

Operational runbook snippets (for on-call):
- If 1m_peak exceeds provisioned capacity by > headroom_pct:
  1) Verify metrics ingestion – look at 1m/5m chart and recent autoscale events.
  2) If autoscaler is stalled, flip to manual scale to nearest even slice count + enable prewarm.
  3) Notify Product on potential degraded responses (channel #prod-hosted-api-alerts).
  4) Kick off temporary cross-region spill if configured (follow spill playbook).

Cost assumptions (for rough dollars):
- Hourly cost: H100 slice equivalent = $10/hr, A100 slice = $6.5/hr, L4 = $2.1/hr (includes infra and amortized software).
- Example: us-west1 13 H100 slices * $10/hr = $130/hr => ~$3,900/day for peak slice capacity (prewarm not included).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate slice tokens/sec numbers against the latest kernel optimizations (see PR #278).
- Do we want headroom expressed as absolute slices instead of percent in small regions? (pro: simpler on-call; con: less adaptive).
- Should prewarm_ratio be per-customer-tier? (enterprise customers get higher prewarm guarantee).
- Create automated alert that computes "delta_to_headroom" and pages SRE only if delta>30% for 3 consecutive minutes.

Quick links / refs: 
- Linked infra ticket: JIRA-INFRA-8421 (metrics/1m/5m ingestion)
- Prewarm design doc draft: CONFLUENCE-1293
- Ingress optimizer PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-optimizer/pull/278

Notes-to-self: keep this sheet short; convert to formal provisioning workbook after ACTION-1 is complete. If we adopt per-customer prewarm tiers, need to re-run sims (Monte Carlo) to quantify cost delta.

Last edited by Asha — will sync with Miguel + Leah before next infra sync.
